summary: The current saved queue identifies synthetic/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst at step 165, now stopping in dog.c:keepdogs() because JavaScript refuses the mounted branch. The source goal is a whole dog.c file-port of mon_leave(), keep_mon_accessible(), and keepdogs(), with every keepdogs caller wired. The selected C step reaches the non-Amulet steed transfer path: clear trap/eating state, drop special carried items, call mon_leave(), move the steed from fmon to gm.mydogs, then restore it after the level changes. This goal covers keepdogs only; dog.c:losedogs() and mon_arrive(With_you) remain separate downstream mounted-transfer blockers, so do not claim this delivery completes the selected screen.

functions: dog.c:mon_leave() (729-762), shared departing-monster bookkeeping; its returned worm segment count is used by both keepdogs() and migrate_to_level().
dog.c:keep_mon_accessible() (768-785), pure classification of the Wizard and level-attached shopkeeper, priest, or vault guard.

dog.c:keepdogs() (789-885), complete departure traversal for both pets_only values, including follower selection, trap/eating/Amulet disposition, steed special-object drop, mydogs transfer, migration routing, and leash cleanup.
source.branch: In the selected recording, the saddled pony is u.usteed, adjacent to the hero, eligible through levl_follower(), not helpless under keepdogs()’s explicit steed exception, and not marked STRAT_WAITFORU. C clears mtrapped and meating, calls mdrop_special_objs(), calls mon_leave(), moves the monster from fmon to gm.mydogs via relmon(), clears mx/my, stores the returned worm segment count in wormno, and records mlstmv. The function then returns to do.c:goto_level(), which continues through the separate losedogs()/mon_arrive(With_you) arrival stage.
callers: do.c:goto_level() (1624) -> js/do.js:goto_level() (2820), already awaits keepdogs(false) during an ordinary level change.
end.c:really_done() (1298) -> js/end.js:really_done() (1346), currently records note_unported("dog.c keepdogs") for ESCAPED/ASCENDED; wire and await keepdogs(true).
wizcmds.c:makemap_remove_mons() (116) -> js/wizcmds.js:makemap_remove_mons() (160), currently records note_unported("dog.c keepdogs"); wire and await keepdogs(true).

dog.c:migrate_to_level() (904) also calls mon_leave() and stores its return in wormno. js/dog.js:migrate_to_level() currently calls mon_leave() but hardcodes wormno=0; preserve the returned segment count at this caller without claiming the rest of migrate_to_level() complete.
dependencies: Direct returned-value helpers already have JavaScript owners: monmove.c:monnear() in js/monmove.js, mondata.c:levl_follower() in js/mondata.js, monst.h:helpless() in js/const.js, wizard.c:mon_has_amulet() in js/wizard.js, and worm.c:count_wsegs() in js/worm.js. count_wsegs() is the only direct helper in mon_leave() whose result is used; its hidden-head exclusion is pinned in scripts/worm.test.mjs.

Direct state-changing helpers have current owners: trap.c:mintrap() in js/trap_effects.js (async, so await it even though C discards its result), apply.c:m_unleash() in js/apply.js, steal.c:mdrop_special_objs() in js/steal.js, worm.c:wormgone() in js/worm.js, monst.c:place_monster() in js/monst.js, and shk.c:set_residency()/picked_container() in js/shk.js.

C relmon() is a void mon.c callee. js/dog.js currently carries the migration-specific adapter for removing ordinary monsters from the live level list and linking them to gm.mydogs or gm.migrating_mons. Keep that existing boundary explicit; mon.c:mon_leaving_level() has broader unstuck, mimic reveal, worm, pit, and redraw effects that are not all represented by the adapter.

keepdogs() calls dog.c:migrate_to_level() as a void result for inaccessible monsters. Its JavaScript implementation is partial; do not claim that function complete in this goal. Preserve an explicit note_unported gap and skip unsupported migration branches instead of treating a partial helper as complete.

The next level-arrival call chain is separate: do.c:goto_level() calls dog.c:losedogs(), which calls dog.c:mon_arrive(With_you). Current js/dog.js rejects a mounted steed in mon_arrive(). Keep this as a downstream blocker; do not widen this goal to losedogs() or the other mon_arrive modes.

scripts/dodown.test.mjs: source caller / goto_level ordinary level-change wiring.
scripts/makemap-remove-mons.test.mjs and scripts/wizcmds.test.mjs: pets_only=true map-removal caller wiring.
